messages:
Cheng: Heads up — saw a spike in GPU pod evictions in the hosted-gpu-pool for us-west2 around 13:02 UTC. Some tenants\' training jobs got bounced.
Marta: any pattern? specific node groups or tenants?
Cheng: Mostly bursty training jobs from tenant 'nbx'. They landed on shared nodes with multiple tenants. autoscaler scaled but nodes were preemptible/spot and we saw OOMKills.
Sam: can you paste the node/pod outputs?
Cheng: ```
$ kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=hosted-gpu-pool -o wide
NAME                          STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE
gke-hosted-gpu-pool-1         Ready    <none>   12d   v1.25.4   10.128.0.12                 Ubuntu 20.04
gke-hosted-gpu-pool-2         Ready    <none>   1h    v1.25.4   10.128.0.31                 Ubuntu 20.04
``` 
Cheng: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n nbx -o wide
NAME                            READY   STATUS    NODE                          RESTARTS
trainer-xyz-0                   0/1     Evicted   gke-hosted-gpu-pool-1         0
trainer-abc-0                   1/1     Running   gke-hosted-gpu-pool-2         0
``` 
Julia: looks like noisy neighbor + spot eviction. Two angles: infra (node-level isolation) and scheduler (pod QoS/priority).
Derrick: we should discuss dedicated node pools per high-cost tenants. Taints + tolerations + nodeSelector will give isolation. cheap option: namespace quota + guaranteed pods + priority classes.
Marta: agree. but dedicated pools increase costs. For high SLO customers it\'s fine; for some mid-size tenants we could use tainted shared pools with strict resource requests to reduce interference.
Sam: cluster-autoscaler config we use currently: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--balance-similar-node-groups` — but it won't scale down if POD disruption budgets or local storage present.
Cheng: also saw cluster-autoscaler logs complaining about scale-up limits: ```I0713 13:05:10 scale_up.go:... : reached quota for group hosted-gpu-pool-us-west2```
Marta: region constraints matter too — us-west2 has limited GPU quota, so dedicated pools might require reserved capacity (committed nodes) in that region.
Derrick: quick prototype idea:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: nbx
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: trainer
  namespace: nbx
spec:
  containers:
  - name: job
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  tolerations:
  - key: 'dedicated'
    operator: 'Equal'
    value: 'gpu-heavy'
    effect: 'NoSchedule'
```
Put those pods on a node pool tainted with `dedicated=gpu-heavy:NoSchedule`.
Julia: also add a PriorityClass for job-critical workloads so they preempt lower-priority ones rather than thrash.
Sam: operational checklist:
- build small dedicated pool (min 2 nodes) in us-west2 for nbx
- taint pool, update tenant deployment to tolerate
- enable eviction alerts and add to dashboard
- evaluate P95 latency and avg cost per token for a week
Marta: cost tradeoffs — if we reserve committed nodes we can sign a lower hourly rate vs on-demand. Ops should prepare a short cost calc.
Cheng: I\'ll spin up the prototype later today and run a couple of synthetic runs. tagging @Derrick for infra changes and @Marta for cost.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026 updated: mitigation plan added (prototype dedicated pool for nbx) :information_source: 
Derrick: acked. I\'ll prepare terraform change for a new node pool with taints + autoscaler group. Will push as a PR to infra repos and include terraform plan output.
Marta: :thumbsup: if prototype looks good let\'s move to a policy doc: when to allocate dedicated pools vs strict shared pools (thresholds: sustained GPU hours per week, SLO importance, regulatory needs).
Cheng: sounds good. I\'ll post results here once the prototype runs finish.
Julia: one more: add a nightly job to run the scheduler-sim tests against the cluster-autoscaler config so we don\'t regress.
Sam: sweet. Thanks all.
